newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW-Swedish Riksbank's inflation report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Swedish Riksbank's inflation report.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Thursday in its quarterly inflation report that the outlook for low inflation was largely unchanged, forecasting underlying inflation at between 1.5-2.0 percent for 1997 and 1998.
However it slightly raised its forecasts for the consumer price index made in March, to about one percent for 1997 and two percent for 1998.
Some analyst comments on the report follows.
"This looks fairly neutral for the market. The inflation forecast is line with target.
They have raised the crown rate from 119 (on the trade-weighted TCW index), which looks a bit positive. They don't seem to emphasise on the crown too much."
"This was completely according to plan. They point out the fact that the economy is gradually strengthening but that this doesn't cause them to worry about inflation.
A higher growth rate at the start of 1999 doesn't seem to lead to any large lack of capacity with the current capacity utilisation.
A rate hike will therefore not be around the corner for quite a while."
